newsitem.title: USA: US junk bonds end up, Smith's Food key gainer.
newsitem.headline: US junk bonds end up, Smith's Food key gainer.

text.p: Corporate high-yield bond prices ended 1/4 to 1/2 higher in relatively moderate volume, however, players said bonds of Smith's Food & Drug Centers were key gainers on the day.
"Smith's Food 11-1/4 bonds gained four points to trade at 116-3/8 bid on the positive news," said one trader.
Players said news that general merchandise retailer, Fred Meyer Inc would buy the supermarket chain boosted the debt, traders said.
Meyer will assume about $1.3 billion of Smith's Food debt in the acquisition.

The Portland, Oregon-based Fred Meyer, which sells food, jewlry, clothing and other items, said on Monday it had signed a definiitive agreeement to acquire Smith's Food in a stock swap valued at about $720 million. The merger will give the combined company 265 stores in 11 states.
Among other supermarket sector issues, Farm Fresh paper traded up a point to 82-1/2 bid, 84-1/2 offer on takeover rumors, traders said.
"The bonds traded up on the rumors...we saw a quote on the offered side today which was unusual," said one high-yield trader.
Ralphs Grocery Co 10.45 and 11 percent bonds were also stronger by 1/2 point, traders added.
Among other junk sector issues, bonds of the largest U.S. paging firm, Paging Network Inc, also posted gains, traders said.
"PageNet's bonds were stronger by a point across the baord," another high-yield trader said.
Turning secondary market for high-grade issues, activity remained quiet as most of the focus remained on the primary sector, traders said.
Despite the pricing of two new debt offerings on Monday, all eyes remain focused on Norfolk Southern's Corp's $3 to $4 billion mega-debt offering this week, players said.
"I think most players are focused on Norfolk Southern's deal," said one high-grade trader.
The deal is expected to consist of five-year, 10-year, 30-year and 40-year, put seven-year securities. Merrill Lynch & Co and JP Morgan Securities will serve as joint lead managers on the deal.

In the overall high-grade sector spreads to U.S. Treasuries remained mostly unchanged, traders said. Meanwhile, on Monday, Suntrust Banks Inc sold $350 million in A1/A-minus rated 30-year flating rate notes to yield a spread of 73 basis points over three-month libor via underwriter Lehman Brothers.
The deal was increased from an initial size of $300 million, Lehman said.
Also, Lowe's Cos issued $100 million in 40-year notes, putable in the 10th and 20th years, to yield 45 basis points over Treasuries. Merrill Lynch was lead manager for the deal.
Meanwhile, the new issue market for high-yield debt is expected to very active this week with 13 new deals totalling roughly $2.5 billion expected to come to market, dealers said.

The largest deals include a $470 million offering of four-year senior discount notes from a holding company of Coleman Co Inc and a $500 million offering of seven-year and 10-year notes from Owens-Illinois Inc.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed up 2/32 at 96-22/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
